extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, CRU (Central Reexamination Unit) support staff, and Technology Center Quality Assurance Specialists involved in ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Operational procedures and substantive requirements for USPTO examiners and support staff to prepare, review, and conclude ex parte reexamination proceedings, including issuance of the Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate and the reexamination certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner litigation investigation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner is responsible for conducting a reasonable investigation for evidence as to whether the patent ... has been or is involved in litigation. The investigation will include a review of the reexamination file, the patent file, and the results of the litigation computer search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If litigation or a federal court decision on the patent is discovered at any time during the reexamination proceeding, the examiner must bring the fact to the attention of the CRU SPRS or TC QAS prior to any further action. The CRU SPRS or TC QAS must review any action taken by the examiner to ensure current Office litigation policy is followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal court decision controlling
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a federal court has ruled upon the merits of a patent and an ex parte reexamination is still appropriate ... the federal court decision will be considered controlling and will be followed as to claims finally held to be invalid by the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims are finally held invalid by a court, follow that decision in the reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with PTAB Review Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: During the pendency of an inter partes review, post grant review or covered business method review ('PTAB Review Proceeding'), the Director may determine how the PTAB Review and the other proceeding may proceed, including providing for stay, transfer, consolidation, or termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an examiner becomes aware of a PTAB Review Proceeding for the same patent being reexamined, the ex parte reexamination proceeding must be referred to the examiner's SPRS. The SPRS will coordinate with the PTAB before taking any action on the reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory decision timeline for reexamination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The existence of a PTAB Review Proceeding does not change the fact that any reexamination request must, by statute, be decided (a grant or a denial) within three months of its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must observe the three-month statutory decision window for ordering or denying reexamination requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of NIRC and Examiner's Amendment upon conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon conclusion of the ex parte reexamination proceeding, the examiner must prepare a 'Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate' (NIRC) ... If appropriate, an examiner's amendment will also be prepared. Where claims are found patentable, reasons must be given for each claim found patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare the reexamination file so Office of Data Management can prepare and issue a certificate under 35 U.S.C. 307 and 37 CFR 1.570. See MPEP § 2288 for certificate issuance steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review conference before issuing NIRC
rubrics_metrics.description: The CRU SPRS/TC QAS will convene a panel review conference, and conference members will review the patentability of the claim(s). If the conference confirms the examiner's decision, a NIRC shall be issued and signed by the examiner, with the two, or more, other conferees initialing the NIRC to indicate their participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All conferees will initial even if one dissented. If the conference does not confirm patentability, the examiner will reevaluate and issue an appropriate Office action rejecting the claim(s) not confirmed as patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to panel review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel review conference is not to be held as to any claim that was in the case (proceeding) at the time the case was reviewed by the Board or a federal court. A panel review conference is not to be held where the proceeding is to be concluded by the cancellation of all claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel review is required in each instance where a NIRC is about to be issued unless (A) the NIRC follows and is consistent with a decision by the Board (or court) on the merits; or (B) the NIRC is issued as consequence of the patent owner's failure to respond where all claims will be canceled.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIRC effect and post-NIRC filings rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A NIRC informs the patent owner and any third party requester that the reexamination prosecution has been terminated. The rules do not provide for an amendment to be filed in a reexamination proceeding after prosecution has been terminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment, information disclosure statement, or other paper related to the merits filed after prosecution has been terminated must be accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to have it considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate issuance when all claims disclaimed
rubrics_metrics.description: If all of the claims are disclaimed in a patent under reexamination, a certificate under 37 CFR 1.570 will be issued indicating that fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where all claims are canceled and a certificate issues, no further Office proceedings will be conducted with that patent or related reissue applications or reexamination requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFW Search Notes form completion
rubrics_metrics.description: The IFW file wrapper Search Notes form — The 'SEARCHED' and the 'SEARCH NOTES' boxes are to be filled in with the classes and subclasses that were actually searched and other areas consulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 719.05 for search documentation guidance; ensure accurate and complete search notes in file.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFW Jacket form completion and litigation/copending boxes
rubrics_metrics.description: The IFW file jacket form — Check to be sure that the necessary data is included thereon, such as the certificate number, e.g., 'C1' or 'C2'. The 'Litigation Review' and 'Copending Office Proceedings' boxes should be completed to ensure that the Office is aware of prior or concurrent litigation and Office proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete jacket form fully to reflect litigation status and copending matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic Data Sheet accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bibliographic Data Sheet — Check to be sure that the data included thereon is correct and the blank spaces have been initialed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify bibliographic data and initial blanks before forwarding for certificate preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue Classification IFW form completion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Issue Classification IFW form — The form must be completed to set forth the status of each claim and the final claim numbers. The appropriate information must be included in the 'Issue Classification' boxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter classification corresponding to current patent classification and any additional classification based on newly claimed subject matter. Completion required even if all claims are canceled. Current classification may be found in PE2E SEARCH (see MPEP § 902.03(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of drawing figure and representative claim for Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: An appropriate drawing figure is to be indicated for printing on the certificate cover sheet and in the Official Gazette. In addition, a representative claim which has been reexamined is to be indicated for publication in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the broadest claim. Examiners should ordinarily designate but one claim on each invention; in reexamination the examiner must select only one claim. A dependent claim should not be selected unless the independent claim from which it depends is also printed; special rules apply for multiple dependent and reissue claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording claim numbers and renumbering rule
rubrics_metrics.description: When recording this information in the box provided, enter the claim number clearly; if multiple claims are selected, separate claim numbers by commas; the claim designated must be referred to by using the renumbered patent claim number rather than the original claim number if different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the renumbering as reflected in the reexamination file; be precise to avoid misidentification on the certificate/Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing attorney/agent names on certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner desires the names of the attorneys or agents, or law firm, to be printed on the certificate, a separate paper limited to this issue which lists the names and positively states that they should be printed on the certificate must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mere power of attorney or change of address is not a request that the name appear on the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner checklist (PTO-1516) completion
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must also complete a checklist, form PTO-1516, for the reexamination file which will be forwarded to the Office of Data Management identifying information used in printing the reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain the form or guidance from CRU SPRS or TC QAS or support staff. Ensure accuracy of responses affecting certificate printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRU support staff clerk checklist (PTO-1517) and data updates
rubrics_metrics.description: After the examiner has prepared the NIRC ... the reexamination and patent files will be given to the CRU support staff. The CRU support staff will complete the Reexamination Clerk Checklist form PTO-1517; the clerk should check to see if any changes in title, inventor, assignee, continuing data, foreign priority, attorney address, and the requester's address have been properly entered and in the Patent Data Portal database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After processing, the clerk will forward the reexamination proceeding to the CRU SPRS or TC QAS for review and approval before processing the NIRC for mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when all claims are canceled — confirmation contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to canceling the claims and issuing the NIRC, the examiner should telephone the patent owner to inquire if a timely response, timely appeal, etc., was filed ... so as to make certain that a timely response has not been misdirected within the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner indicates no such filing or cannot be reached, proceed to issue a NIRC terminating prosecution. If contacted, make the telephone interview of record as attachment to the NIRC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting examiner's amendment canceling all claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proceeding is to be concluded by the cancellation of all claims, the examiner will issue a NIRC action, and as an attachment to the NIRC, the examiner will draft an examiner's amendment canceling all live claims in the reexamination proceeding. In the examiner's amendment, the examiner should point out why the claims have been canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific explanatory statements (examples are provided in MPEP) referencing the Office action dates, Board decisions, and applicable CFR and MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of representative canceled patent claim for Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner will designate a cancelled original patent claim to be printed in the Official Gazette when all claims are canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the chosen canceled claim in the Issue Classification IFW form appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of multiple dependent claims in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purpose of the NIRC, the addition of a claim of the multiple dependency is viewed as adding a new claim ... the deletion of a claim of the multiple dependency is viewed as canceling the claim deleted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For certificate printing and the Examiner's checklist, additions/deletions of multiple dependency elements are often treated as amended claims (printed in amended form), while new dependency-based claims may be designated as 'new' and deleted ones as 'canceled'; provide clear mapping of pre- and post-reexamination designations (examples given in MPEP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim status reporting on Examiner's checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete Examiner's checklist items to indicate which patent claims are confirmed, amended, canceled, dependent on amended, and new claims patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific entries and example formatting in the MPEP to populate checklist items (e.g., Patent claims confirmed: 1, 5, 7; Patent claims amended: 2, 3, 4 and 6; New claims patentable: 8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminder — examine all claims with SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: All patent claims for which a substantial new question of patentability has been found must have been examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure examination coverage for each claim implicated by the substantial new question; see MPEP § 2243.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminder — renumbering rule
rubrics_metrics.description: No renumbering of patent claims is permitted. New claims may require renumbering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the MPEP guidance and CFR on renumbering — be careful to use renumbered patent claim numbers when recording for the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminder — amendment formatting and multiple amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments to the description and claims must conform to requirements of 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j). If a portion of the text is amended more than once, each amendment should indicate all of the changes (insertions and deletions) in relation to the current text in the patent under reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 2250 for specific marking and presentation requirements; examiner's amendment must meet the same rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminder — prior art listing format
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior art must be listed on a form PTO 892, PTO/SB/08, or PTO/SB/42 (or on a form having a format equivalent to one of these forms). These forms must be properly completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2257 for details on prior art listing and required fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminder — completion and cross-check of PTO-1516 and PTO-1517
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner and reexamination clerk checklists PTO-1516 and PTO-1517 must be entirely and properly completed. A careful reading of the instructions contained in these checklists is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The clerical checklist is designed to check and review the examiner's responses; CRU support staff should personally review the file and ensure responses on both checklists agree before final processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminder — merging pending proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple pending reexamination proceedings are often merged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2283 for criteria and processing instructions for merging reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminder — copending reissue consideration by OPLA
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the reexamination proceeding is copending with an application for reissue of the patent being reexamined, the files must have been forwarded to the Office of Patent Legal Administration (OPLA) for a consideration of potential merger, with a decision (by a Senior Legal Advisor) on the question being present in the reexamination file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure OPLA disposition is in the file prior to issuing NIRC/certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminder — reasons for patentability required
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons for patentability and/or confirmation are required for each claim found patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear reasons in an attachment to the NIRC explaining why the claims are patentable over cited patents or publications; see guidance below for forms and phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminder — no issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no issue fee in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assess or collect an issue fee for reexamination certificates (see MPEP § 2233).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminder — claims post-expiration
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent claims may not be amended nor new claims added after expiration of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 2250 for restrictions; if patent has expired, amendments and added claims must be withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminder — drawings and figure rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Original drawings cannot be physically changed. 'Amended' or 'New' figures must be appropriately labeled as such and presented on new sheets in compliance with 37 CFR 1.84 and 37 CFR 1.530(d)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure any new or amended figures comply with drawing rules and are properly labeled and submitted on new sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminder — amended/new claims may not enlarge scope
rubrics_metrics.description: An amended or new claim may not enlarge the scope of the patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all claim amendments narrow or maintain scope relative to the patent as issued; see MPEP § 2250.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminder — effects when patent expired during proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent has expired, all amendments to the patent claims and all claims added during the proceeding must be withdrawn. Further, all presently rejected and objected-to claims are canceled by examiner's amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a statement in the examiner's amendment withdrawing such changes (sample language provided in MPEP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendment formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner's amendment is prepared, the examiner's amendment must comply with the requirements of 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) in amending the patent. The exception for examiner's amendments set forth in 37 CFR 1.121(g) does not apply to examiner's amendments in reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present full text of any paragraph or claim to be changed, with 37 CFR 1.530(f) markings. The only exception is that an entire claim or an entire paragraph may be deleted by a statement deleting the claim or paragraph without presentation of the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title/abstract change rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally the title of the invention or the abstract will not need to be changed ... If a change to the title or to the abstract is necessary, the patent owner should be notified of the need to provide an amendment changing the title or abstract as early as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all claims are found patentable and a NIRC has been or is to be mailed, the examiner may only change the title or abstract by an examiner's amendment authorized by the patent owner. Changing the title by merely initialing the change is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement when patent expires during pendency — withdrawal statement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent expires during the pendency of a reexamination proceeding for that patent, all amendments to the patent claims and all claims added during the proceeding must be withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner's amendment is to include a statement such as: 'As the patent being reexamined has expired during the pendency of the reexamination proceeding, all amendments made during the proceeding are improper, and are hereby expressly withdrawn.'

rubrics_metrics.name: PTOL-469 Box 7 and form paragraph 22.06 for examiner's amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner's amendment is prepared, Box 7 of form PTOL-469 (NIRC) is checked, and form paragraph 22.06 is used to provide the appropriate attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the examiner's amendment text and use the prescribed form paragraph to notify patent owner of the changes reflected in the forthcoming certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for patentability and/or confirmation preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the attachment to the NIRC, the examiner should indicate why the claims found patentable in the reexamination proceeding are clearly patentable over the cited patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set forth reasons similar to those used for allowance in an application (see MPEP § 1302.14). May use form PTOL-476 or form paragraph 22.16 ('Statement of Reasons for Patentability and/or Confirmation'). Where the record is clear, examiner may refer to particular portions of the record which establish patentability. Any comments by the patent owner must be labeled and will be placed in the reexamination file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and terminology for confirmed vs patentable claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Original patent claims that are found patentable in a reexamination proceeding are generally to be designated as 'confirmed' claims, while new claims and amended patent claims are generally to be designated as 'patentable' claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of setting forth reasons, the examiner may use 'patentable' to refer to any claim that defines over the cited patents or printed publications; there is no need to separate 'confirmed' and 'patentable' categories when stating reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions after NIRC — petition requirement under 37 CFR 1.182
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules do not provide for an amendment to be filed in a reexamination proceeding after a NIRC has been issued. Any amendment, information disclosure statement, or other paper related to the merits of the reexamination proceeding filed after the NIRC must be accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.182.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petition is granted, the examiner will reconsider the case in view of the new information and, if appropriate, reopen prosecution. See MPEP § 2256 for criteria for entry and consideration of IDS filed after a NIRC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of comments on statement of reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Any 'Comments on Statement of Reasons for Patentability and/or Confirmation' which are received will be placed in the reexamination file, without comment. This will be done even when the reexamination certificate has already issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner comments are docketed and preserved in the file but not substantively annotated by the examiner in the certificate process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in ex parte reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination certificate will set forth the results of the proceeding and the content of the patent following the reexamination proceeding. The certificate will: (A) cancel any patent claims determined to be unpatentable; (B) confirm any patent claims determined to be patentable; (C) incorporate into the patent any amended or new claims determined to be patentable; (D) make any changes in the description approved during reexamination; (E) include any statutory disclaimer or terminal disclaimer filed by the patent owner; (F) identify unamended claims which were held invalid on final holding by another forum on any grounds; (G) identify any patent claims not reexamined; (H) be mailed on the day it is dated to the patent owner and a copy mailed to the third party requester; and (I) identify patent claims, dependent on amended claims, determined to be patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 35 U.S.C. 307 and 37 CFR 1.570; ensure certificate language accurately reflects claim dispositions and any changes to the specification, disclaimers, and claim dependencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of certificate canceling all claims and rare reissue exception
rubrics_metrics.description: If a certificate issues and publishes which cancels all of the claims of the patent, no further Office proceedings will be conducted with regard to that patent or any reissue application or reexamination request directed thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In rare situations where a reissue application is copending, the patent owner may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 requesting waiver of 37 CFR 1.570(d) to address claims pending in the reissue application; such petition must be accompanied by a paper cancelling any claim within the scope of the claims canceled by the certificate and explaining why remaining claims are patentable over canceled claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of certificate issuance in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of the issuance of each reexamination certificate will be published in the Official Gazette on its date of issuance in a format similar to that used for reissue patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate selection of representative claim and figure for Official Gazette publication as previously instructed.
